messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] KV cache memory growth detected on serve-group:us-west-2 (auto-threshold). Spike in kv_cache.entries and tail latency. Link: https://grafana.redwood/example/d/Q0Kv/cache-spike
alex (oncall): Ack. Paging eng-sre and runtime. Impacting gen-latency p95, some 503s.
sara: I’m seeing a sustained ramp starting ~2125001000. KV entries up 12x, mem usage +65%. Correlated with speculative_decode=true rollout to canary pool.
miguel: hmm, yeah speculative decode enables draft/target tracking which pins more KV contexts, and continuous batching is keeping drafts in flight longer — could cause cache churn.
priya: Any customer-facing errors?
alex (oncall): Yes — small set of high-throughput customers in prod-US seeing increased 5xxs and slow responses for streaming. Tickets from two customers. Severity: P2 -> P1 if not mitigated in 30m.
sara: Quick triage: let's reduce batch size and disable speculative decode on canary immediately. Also raise eviction aggressiveness on KV cache to free memory.
miguel: Agreed. Plan: 1) set speculative_decode=false for canary model group 2) set batch.max_tokens=256 (was 2048) 3) set kv_cache.max_entries=200000 and kv_cache.eviction_ms=30000.
priya: I'll coordinate routing to divert traffic away from canary if we need a full rollback.
ops-bot: Runbooks: incident/kv-cache-throttle -> https://wiki.redwood/incident/kv-cache-throttle
alex (oncall): Execute step 1 now. miguel, can you push the flag?
miguel: Pushing now. Command: ```
# disable speculative decode on canary
redctl rollout set --pool canary --model-group gen-llama --speculative_decode false
```
ops-bot: rollout job queued -> job-id=rb-8943. Estimated apply 12s.
ops-bot: rollout job finished -> rb-8943 SUCCESS on 3/3 nodes.
sara: Good. Next reduce batch size: miguel, go ahead.
miguel: Applying batch config change: ```
redctl config set --scope cluster --key batch.max_tokens --value 256
redctl config set --scope cluster --key batch.max_requests --value 8
```
ops-bot: config apply SUCCESS. Changes propagated to serving runtime.
sara: Updating KV cache params: ```
redctl config set --scope cluster --key kv_cache.max_entries --value 200000
redctl config set --scope cluster --key kv_cache.eviction_ms --value 30000
```
ops-bot: config apply SUCCESS. Eviction sampler kicked.
priya: Routing hold: temporarily divert 30% of traffic from canary to stable pool to alleviate pressure. `routectl shift --from canary --to stable --pct 30`
alex (oncall): Noted. Watching metrics.
(1m) sara: p95 generation latency dropping from 1.8s -> 1.1s. KV entries trending down. Error rate still elevated but falling.
(4m) miguel: Memory usage on serving nodes decreased ~40%. No new 503s reported in the last 3m.
alex (oncall): Customer update draft: "We've applied an emergency mitigation that rolled back a canary decode optimization and tuned batching to restore stability. We're monitoring and will post a full postmortem." Approve? :thumbsup:
sara: +1. Keep monitoring for 30m before closing. Also capture traces for draft/target divergence during the window.
miguel: I've grabbed a few heap dumps and KV cache histograms; saving to s3: s3://incidents/2125001234/kvcache-dumps.tgz
priya: I'll open a follow-up to revert canary gradual rollout until we validate cache pressure under continuous batching.
ops-bot: Created incident doc -> https://incidents.redwood/2125001234 (auto).
alex (oncall): Handoff: I'm staying until stabilization. If metrics hold for 30m, handoff to sara for follow-up tuning and postmortem. Checklist: 1) confirm customer ticket updates 2) collect eval prompt sets that triggered divergence 3) schedule postmortem.
sara: A couple of notes for postmortem: - quantify how speculative decode pins draft/target contexts - simulate with load test to reproduce KV churn - consider adaptive eviction tied to speculative_load metric
miguel: Longer-term options: bound per-session kv entries, add lightweight refs instead of full context for speculative drafts, and make continuous batching aware of speculative ownership windows.
priya: Customer impact summary for ticketing: ~2 customers, 3-5 minute error bursts, degradation window 2125000900-2125001600, mitigated at ~2125001200.
alex (oncall): Marking incident as mitigated. We'll keep monitoring for 1h. If anything else crops up, re-open. Thanks all. :heart:
sara: Adding follow-up tasks to backlog: KVC-1124 (adaptive eviction), RUNTIME-879 (speculative per-request cap), POST-212500 (writeup).
ops-bot: Incident state -> MITIGATED. Closed alerts: alert-id=kv-cache-spike-5412.
(55m) alex (oncall): Metrics stable, memory normalized, error rate back to baseline. Handoff complete -> sara is follow-up owner.
sara: Acknowledged handoff. I'll coordinate the postmortem and link artifacts.
